verdict: A spend interruption mid-week slowed volume; overdue infrastructure is being resolved.
narrative: This period, MedStation received 99 leads across 28 days at a cost of $5.36 per lead — but the last 7 days told a sharper story: spend dropped 45% and leads fell 50% versus the prior 7 days, traced directly to three consecutive zero-spend days (September 24–26), not a change in audience or creative performance. Local visibility followed the same pattern, with Google Business Profile actions falling sharply in the same window as paid activity paused. A set of foundational build-outs — including search campaigns, lead-nurture sequences, and local search verification — that were scoped for July through September remain undelivered, and completing those is the single highest-priority item heading into October. Once spend resumes consistently and the infrastructure milestones are closed, volume should recover to and beyond the earlier-September pace.

watch_item.issue: Spend went to zero for three days (Sep 24–26), pulling weekly lead volume down 50% and pushing cost per lead up 9%.
watch_item.fix: Spend has resumed and the budget interruption is being addressed to prevent recurrence; the overdue campaign infrastructure is being prioritized for completion this week ahead of the Phase 1 close.
